title: A puzzle game's description, or a library of techniques
description: What `src/describe/load.ts` validates every `*.description.yaml` against. Every string marked a formula is in the formula syntax of docs/descriptions.md § "The formula syntax", and the compiler parses each. Every string marked prose is markdown.

firstCells.description: A value dealt first on the share of the cells option `share` gives, as a percentage, as symmetric as option `symmetry` asks (upstream's set_blacks, the choices none, 2-way mirror, 2-way rotational, 4-way mirror and 4-way rotational).

ramp.description: After each `every` draws the share goes up `step`, and past `top` starts over from the params' own: a layout few boards of the tier come from is left behind (upstream lightup.c's ramp of walls).

saidMark.description: A set of elements, or where the step marks elements of several sorts in one role, a set of each by its sort's name (`{ face: "{f}", cell: "{c}" }`), or `{ supplied: elements }` where only the game's code can find them.

saidTerm.description: A formula over the binding, or a term only the game's code can know, by its kind: the game's hook for the technique returns it (`SuppliedById` in the compiled module), and a wording's `when` cannot read it. `words` is a list of words said as they are: `{term}` as a list, `{either term}` as alternatives, `{term: one | several}` by how many. `several` is the engine's: whether the step decides more than one element, over all its legs.

saidTerms.description: Named values the step's sentence reads, by name.

saidMarks.description: The elements a step marks, by the role they are marked in. The firing's own facts are ringed without being said; evidence is the outline's set less them.

clause.description: A part of a hint step's sentence, whole, with slots: `{term}`, `{word}`, `{role}`, `{role: one | several}`, `{role term: words}` (`engine/hint/stated.ts`).

wordings.description: The same deduction said for what the board shows: tried in order, the first whose `when` holds giving the step its clauses, a part it leaves out taken from the clauses beside the list. A firing's `when` reads the binding, the terms, and the marks by role. Only the last may leave out `when`.

long.description: Why this wording may run past the line a hint's sentence keeps to (`NARRATION_LIMIT`), which the hint walk then lets it. On a part it covers every wording the part states. `npm run describe` refuses one on wordings that cannot run past the line, and asks for one on a wording past it on every board.

rung.description: The game's hint rungs a firing of this is recorded under, among its hintRungs: one, or several where one firing records under more than one (an Unequal sign's two ends).

from.description: A tier above the technique's own, on its scale: the ladder runs it only at a cap that high, and a firing grades at its own tier. Solo's reading of the partial cages the region rule works out grades as a cage's reading, and only where the region rule is in reach.

until.description: A tier above the technique's own: at a cap that high the ladder does not run it, where a technique there strikes all it does and a grade should not rest on the weaker one.

statement.description: What a technique says, wherever it is stated.

on.description: The engine runs it as each value is placed (`place`), or as a fact strikes a value from a cell (`strike`), with its first binder bound to that cell, and not as a rung of the ladder. One run on striking only strikes.

for.description: The binders, as after `forall`: `x in S where P, y = t, ...`.

premise.description: Over the marks; absent is true.

conclude.description: `strike(c, d)` and `place(c, d)` facts, joined by `and`, under `forall` where it ranges.

says.description: What a hint step for a firing of this speaks of, each a formula over the technique's binding, read on the marks before the firing's facts are made (under the technique's own `with`).

shown.description: `each`: a step for every square the firing decides, each its own argument (its evidence is the outline less that square alone). `legs`: the same, the steps after the first continuing it. `value`: on a board of notes, a step for every value the firing strikes, from all the squares it strikes it in (Towers' heights). Absent, one step for the firing.

witness.description: Report, with the firing, what held in its `for ... where` and `premise`: the arm of an `or` that held, the member an `exists` held for, the supposition a `with` made, and each definition read. Read on a hint's path only.

reads.description: Report, with the firing, the elements whose marks its `for ... where` and `premise` read (`reads.cells`, `reads.edges`), for the engine to find what the firing rests on. Read on a hint's path only.

again.description: A later leg of a journey (`shown: legs`): said after its move in place of `look` and `follows`, the reasoning the first leg gave as this square adds to it.

later.description: What a later leg says as its move, in place of `move`, where it differs; said with the `again` relation.

fact.description: What a square the firing decides has of its own, read where the conclusion's `place` or `strike` makes it, in the conclusion's scope (a `forall` binder is live, and a `with` may be written): the step for that square takes these in place of the firing's, and a step for the firing takes the union of its squares' marks.

wordings.description: Where a square's step reads differently by what holds where its fact is made, each `when` read in the conclusion's scope.

arms.description: Where a step reads differently by what holds of the binding: each arm is a name and a condition, tried in order, the first true one winning, and adds its own `terms` and `marks` to the shared ones above. The step's kind is `<id>.<arm>`.

tier.description: One of `tiers`, or of one of `scales`.

oneOf.description: A library's technique placed at a tier of this game's.
A kind of rule's technique (`src/describe/kinds.ts`), filled in with this game's nouns.

as.description: The technique's id in this game.

says.description: The game's own words, laid over what the kind brings; the technique it expands into is checked against the statement's `says`. `false` places the kind without words, for a game whose hint narrates the firing itself.

library.description: Techniques stated once, for every game that places them with `use`.

outside.description: The one-valued clue kind at a cell that each cell of the store outside the hexagon holds: dealt there and nowhere else, and never written in the desc.

hexagon.description: The board is a hexagon `w` cells wide and `h` high, each row half a cell right of the one below, stored as upstream's unreleased bricks.c does: a grid half its height wider, its two corners outside. It is drawn sheared, the pointer and the arrows read it so, and the numpad's 7, 9, 1 and 3 step along its diagonals.

slots.description: One slot beyond each end of every row and column, seeing along it: `slots`, `sight(s)`, `opposite(s)`.

edges.description: The orthogonal pairs: `edges`, `ends(e)`, `end1(e)`, `end2(e)`, `other(e, c)`, `edge(a, b)`. `king` adds the diagonal pairs, and `crossedBy(e)`, the other diagonal of the four squares a diagonal edge crosses (none for an orthogonal one).

corners.description: Every point inside the grid where four cells meet: `corners`, `cells(k)`, `corners(c)`, `across(k, c)`.

points.description: Every point where cells meet, the border's included: `points`, `cells(k)`, `points(c)`, `slash(c, k)` (the value, 1 or 2, of `c`'s diagonal through `k`), `linked(k)` (the points the cells' diagonals join to `k`).

centers.description: Every center inside the grid a square can be turned about, a square's middle, a side's or a point where four meet: `centers`, `cells(p)` (the squares round it), `opp(c, p)` (the square `c` turns to about `p`, half a turn, or none off the grid).

diagonals.description: The two diagonals of a square grid: `diagonals`.

regions.description: Named partitions of the cells: `dealt`, from the board, or a library partition such as `blocks(rw, rh)`.

relations.description: A planning game's relations the board deals, each a set of cells for each cell, read `name(c)`.

tiling.description: A board that is a tiling the deal decides (Loopy's), in place of `grid`: its cells are the dots, `edges` join them (`edges(c)` a dot's, in its turn), and two sorts of element more, `faces` (`cells(f)` and `edges(f)` round a face, `faces(e)` either side of an edge) and `angles`, two edges side by side round a dot (`angles(c)` a dot's in its turn, `angles(f)` a face's, `edges(a)`, `apex(a)` its dot). Rows, columns, neighbors by direction and coordinates are refused on it. `square` where the tiling is always the grid of squares, the dots its squares (Pearl's): the techniques are checked on square tilings alone.

cells.description: A planning game's board that is not a rectangle: this many cells and no geometry, so `x`, `y`, `cell`, the neighbors, rays and lines are refused on it. In place of `grid`.

faces.description: A planning game's second sort of element: a size the board deals, how many faces. `faces` names them, and a layer `over: faces` holds a value a face.

tables.description: A planning game's tables the board deals, each a function of elements and numbers to an element, `none` where it has no value: read `name(a, ...)`, or `name` where it takes nothing.

units.description: The named sets of lines and regions in which no value repeats: `units`, `units_of(c)` and `peers(c)` read them.

define.description: Named terms and predicates, `name(params)` to a formula.

implied.description: Statements the rules imply, by name, said so a breach shows on a board still being filled: read by the live error check alone.

clues.description: Clue kinds: where one sits, its values, and what it means, reading `at` and `v`.

at.description: The element sort a clue sits at, or `board` for a whole-board clue, which has `fields` in place of a `value`.

per.description: A clue at the element for each value of the answer's domain, read `clue(kind, x, d)`; its meaning reads the value as `per`.

list.description: The clue at an element is a list of numbers, each one of `value`, in order: a line's run lengths. `clue(kind, x)` is the list, and its meaning reads it as `v`.

fields.description: A whole-board clue's parts, each read as a function of the clue, and of an element where it has an `at`: one a cell is `peg(k, s)`.

list.description: The field of a clue is a list of numbers, each one of `value`, in order: a number's digits. Read whole as `f(k)`, its length `|f(k)|`, and a member `nth(f(k), i)`, counted from 0.

complete.description: Every place carries one, so an absent clue is a fact.

domain.description: The values the layer may hold, read by the dead-end checker; `integers` for a domain that is not finite, which holds any integer a double holds exactly and is computed exactly.

checked.description: Of a layer whose domain is `integers`, the values the dead-end checker searches it over: a line of moves that leaves them ends there.

arranged.description: The layer is an arrangement: each value of its domain on this many cells. Read by the dead-end checker.

once.description: Exactly one cell holds this value, and every other another of the domain: a token, such as a ball. Read by the dead-end checker.

on.description: Where this formula of the cell `c`, which reads only layers at `c`, is false, the layer holds 0: a value stands only there. Read by the dead-end checker.

carried.description: A value a move copies and no rule reads, such as a barrel's letter: the compiler refuses a read of it but in an assignment to itself, and the dead-end checker holds it at 0.

over.description: The layer holds a value a face of `space.faces`, or one value for the whole board, read by its name alone, in place of a value a cell.

assignments.description: What a move sets: each entry's binders, the last of them the cell assigned, and a term for each layer it assigns, read on the position before the move. An entry with no binders assigns layers over the board.

deadEnds.description: Claims by id, each a formula over the position true only where no line of moves finishes: `Game.hasNoSolution`. Each is checked sound on small boards.

help.description: The game's help page, which `src/describe/help-page.ts` renders in this order: the title is the catalog's name, and every `#` and `##` heading and `{{parameters}}` are the renderer's.

sections.description: The game's own sections, each under its heading.

origins.description: Who invented the puzzle, its other names, where more of it is: under `## Where the puzzle comes from`, or `puzzles come` for a game with rulesets.

hints.description: Under `## Hints`: what the hint's marks mean here, and its words for them. Present exactly when the game has a hint.

parameters.description: Under `## <Name> parameters`, either side of the list generated from `paramConfig`.

game.description: A game's description: its help page, its formal rules, or both. The formal rules come whole.

then.description: A game's rules state an answer, or a planning game's position and its moves.

game.description: The id, as the app's registry has it, or a family's other game.

produces.description: What the player produces: latin, shading, lines, ... The technique check's `inherit` reads it for the games whose techniques a candidate may share. Not the catalog's family, which is what a player browses by and is the game's `catalog.ts`'s, as is its name.

sizes.description: The numbers the rules are stated over, each a range: the worlds the soundness check builds. Not the Custom dialog's bounds, which the game's `paramConfig` states for the boards it deals. `max` is left out where the rules set none.

step.description: Where the size is a multiple of it alone (Unruly's even sides): a fill game's Custom dialog refuses another.

sort.description: What holds a value: a cell, or the edge between two cells side by side (Separate's walls), where the space has its edges.

wide.description: Whether a value may run past 31, the most a mask of 32 bits holds: Ascent's number on a square, up to the board's square count. A cell's candidates are then read by membership, a count, the least and a binder, never as a set, and the domain is `range(a, b)` or `{d in range(a, b) where P}`.

to.description: The cell a cell's value names, a term of the cell `c` and the value `d`, none where it names none: what `to(c)` reads and `chain(c)` follows. Rome's arrows are `step(c, d)`; Signpost's links `compass(c, clue(arrow, c), d)`.

repeat.description: The one value of the domain that appears more than once in a unit, and how many times: `times(d)` reads it, 1 for every other value. Salad's empty square.

given.description: The answer functions the board may give values of: givens, not clues.

marks.description: What the player can write down.

of.description: For a mark on the edges, on a tiling's angles, or on the cells of an answer that is not on the cells, a technique reads: the number of the answer it narrows, read of the element `at`. The mark is read `name(e)`, the values it may still hold, and narrowed by `strike(e, d)`. On the answer's own elements, `value(at)`: the values each may still hold, which the violation check reads as the element's domain (Bridges' line).

means.description: For a mark on the cells that names one clue (`notation: "one of clues(kind)"`): what the cell `at` naming the clue `v` says of the answer. The mark is read `name(c)`, the clue or none, and made by `mark(c, q)`.

while.description: For the cell mark that names one clue: what it needs to stand, read of the cell `at` on the board's values. An edit drops every mark whose `while` the values it leaves break (Tents' link needs `value(at) = 1`).

breaks.description: How a rule is seen broken, `name(params)` to its clause: `when`, a formula the techniques read as a definition; `look`, the words naming what broke, which a technique's `{broke}` says where this break is the one its witness holds; and `terms`, formulas over the parameters those words read, read on the marks the break was found on (under a supposition where it was read under one).

views.description: A planning game's definitions the game reads beside its rules, each of cells, its last parameter the cell: the compiled module's `views` gives the cells each holds of, for values of the others.

kind.description: For a planning game, `permute` claims every move is legal everywhere and moves the pieces the same way on every position, which the dead-end checker checks; `transition` claims nothing.

position.description: A planning game's position: its layers, each a value a cell, by name, read in a formula as a function of a cell.

moves.description: A planning game's moves, by name, in the order a position's moves are listed.

for.description: Its arguments, as a technique's binders: plain numbers and elements.

when.description: Its guard, over the position; absent is true.

finish.description: Formulas over the position, all true of a finished one.

lose.description: Formulas over the position, any true of a lost one.

play.description: How the player fills the board, for a fill game the engine plays (`engine/fill/play.ts`): each value they place, the two buttons' values, the drag, and the link drawn as the one cell mark.

numbers.description: The values are the answer's domain, a line of numbers: each drawn as its numeral, typed into a selected square by its key (`engine/fill/numbers.ts`). A board played so has no `values` and no buttons.

raised.description: Each value is drawn as a block as tall as it, its top up and right of its square with the numeral on it (upstream towers.c's 3D towers, `engine/render/raised.ts`): a press on a top is its square's, and the player's appearance preference draws them flat. On a board with no gaps and no clues at parts.

hintNotes.description: Where `marks` declares candidate notes, how the hint reads a square with none until the player chooses (the hint-notes preference): `implicit`, as every number its row and column leave it, writing notes only where a step rests on them; `populate`, every candidate penciled in first. `populate` where it is left out (`docs/hints-candidates.md` § "Choosing the default").

gaps.description: The clue kinds at edges, each drawn in a gap between its two cells by the painter named (`engine/render/pieces/edge.ts`): a board with any is drawn with a half-tile gap between every two cells.

done.description: The clue kinds the player may mark done, each with what one is called ("sign"), which the help page's sentence on the mark says (`engine/fill/done.ts`): a press on such a clue, with either button, grays it, a drag on grays those that looked the same, and Shift or Ctrl with an arrow marks the one beside the selected square. Each is a kind drawn in a gap (`gaps`), on a board of `numbers`.

values.description: The values the player places, by the description's value: what its verb does ("place a tent"), the letter that places it, its three-character glyph in the text format, and the painter that draws it.

key.description: The key that places the value, a capital letter or a digit, or a list of them.

given.description: The values only the deal places, a fixed cell's: their glyph and painter.

primary.description: The left button's value, which a click toggles with open.

secondary.description: The right button's value, which rules a cell out.

blank.description: The value an open cell reads as for the answer check, where the answer is the other values alone (Tents' grass).

erase.description: A letter that empties a cell, beside Backspace and Delete.

straight.description: A drag keeps to the row or column it runs along, for a game whose clues are on rows and columns, and one whose values are lines; otherwise it follows the pointer. Either way it gives every square it passes that held what the pressed square held what the pressed square became.

sweepWith.description: The one button whose drag sweeps; the other's drag acts where it began alone (Light Up's bulbs, a row of which light each other). Both sweep where absent.

wash.description: A wash over the open cells where `when` holds of the values, `c` the cell (Light Up's lit squares). An open washed cell reads as the secondary value to the live errors, and a placement's consequences there are what the board shows, so the hint neither makes nor says them. `pref`, where given, is a preference, on by default, that draws the secondary piece on a washed cell; off, it is left out.

hides.description: A value whose piece hides the number on its cell, and a preference, off by default, that shows the number there smaller; a press off the grid flips it (upstream's Singles).

wrap.description: An arrow at the grid's edge carries the cursor to the other edge (upstream's Singles).

tally.description: A board clue of two fields, a length and the count of pieces of it, that the params give: the size by its letter after the grid's (`f3`), the counts after a comma at the end (`,3,2,1`), one of the longest and one more of each shorter by default (upstream's Boats fleet).

single.description: The one tier a tally of one piece is dealt at.

click.description: What a click does: `toggle` (the default) sets the button's value or empties a cell holding it; `cycle` goes round empty, the button's value and the other button's, the right button the other way round.

shape.description: The clue kind at a cell that gives the cell's piece and its shape (Boats' given segments): its domain fixes the cell, which is drawn as its piece, shaped as in the answer, and never as a number.

dealt.description: The clue kind at a cell that the cell is dealt holding: its value is the cell's, which no edit changes. Its meaning is `value(at) = v`, alone or before an `and`; one that says more is drawn with a dot on its piece.

default.description: The default board, one of `boards`, where it is not the first.

defaultTier.description: The tier the default board is dealt at, one the menu offers it at, where it is not the first (upstream's Adjacent, 5x5 Normal where the menu offers 5x5 from Easy).

boardTiers.description: The first and last tier a board of `boards` is offered at, by its `WxH`, where it is not every tier.

sizes.description: Each size beyond the grid's that the rules read, which the params give, by its name in `sizes`: its letter in the params, written as the number itself, and its rulesets, one for each value from the size's `min`, each with the narrowest board it has an answer on (`least`). The Custom dialog offers them as its game mode, and the help's `{{rulesets}}` lists them (Star Battle's stars).

plain.description: The clue kinds written as a number on their cell that are drawn plain: a number whose meaning reads no block of cells (Range's, which sees along its row and column), so it has no block to outline, never turns faint, and is not counted in the status bar.

bounds.description: What the size alone cannot say of a board: bounds on its two sides together, `sum` (w + h), `area` (w × h), `shorter` and `longer`; and in `tiers`, by a tier's name, further bounds on a board of that tier. A board outside them is refused, a tier's as having no such tier.

variants.description: The boards after the menu's grid, one for each modifier: a size of `boards`, the variations on, and its tier.

modifiers.description: Each variation the player may switch on, by its name: its letter in the params, its Custom field (`kw`, `name`), its words in a board's name and the rule the help lists (`engine/game-id/modifier.ts`), and `most`, where the rule bounds the size: a board 2i squares across has at most `most[i]` lines the other way.

links.description: The cell mark naming a clue, drawn as a link between a cell and the clue's cell beside it.

glance.description: The techniques that read a link the board shows at a glance, by id: the hint runs them once on the drawn links before each step, so it never asks for one of those, and asks for a deeper link only where it lets a later technique fire (`engine/hint/glance.ts`). Needs `links`.

askBefore.description: The techniques, by id, before which the hint asks for a deeper link where one lets a technique above them fire. It asks once more after the last technique, for any, and there for a link that lets nothing fire where no link does. Needs `glance`.

signs.description: The sign drawn after the number of each clue kind at a dealt partition's part, by kind (Keen's `+` and `×`): the clue is drawn at the part's first square, its number and its sign, above the notes.

labels.description: Fixed text in the margin, which is not a clue: `start`, before each row and column, a formula of `i`, the line's index along its axis from 0 (Kakurasu's weights, `i + 1`).

boards.description: The sizes the preset menu offers, `WxH`, each followed by the sizes beyond the grid's it gives by their letters (`8x8s2`, two stars; a size it does not name is at its `min`), smallest first, each at every tier unless `boardTiers` says otherwise; the first at the easiest tier is the default board unless `default` names another. A game born from its description (`catalog:`) states them.

hintMarks.description: What each mark of the hint means in this game (`Game.hint.marks`), which the help's `{{hint-marks}}` lists. A game born from its description (`catalog:`) states the roles its steps draw.

catalog.description: A game born from its description: its catalog entry (`engine/contract/catalog.ts`'s `PuzzleData`). The compiler then writes `<id>.catalog.ts` and `<id>.game.ts`, which registers `fillGame` of the compiled module.

collection.description: Typed by `PuzzleData`, which the generated entry is: the typecheck refuses one that is not.

family.description: Typed by `PuzzleData`, which the generated entry is: the typecheck refuses one that is not.

id.description: A fill game's game ID, its segments in order (`engine/fill/game-id.ts`): `runs: <kind>`, the cells a clue kind sits at as upstream's run code (`_`, `a`-`y`, `z`); `numbers: <kind>`, the kind's values, the first after `before` (nothing by default) and each other after a comma, an absent clue written as nothing, in the space's order or with `order: columns` the columns first. Absent, `numbers` of every clue kind in turn, a comma between them.

oneOf.description: A dealt partition as the walls between its parts (`engine/game-id/wall-runs.ts`): every border between two cells side by side, those inside the rows first, a number a run of walls and a letter a run of gaps then a wall.

A list kind at lines, each line's list in turn, its numbers between `.` and the lines between `/`, an empty list written as nothing (upstream's Pattern). With `order: columns`, the columns come first.
A clue kind on every cell, each one character of the desc alphabet (`engine/game-id/desc-alphabet.ts`: `0`–`9`, `a`–`z`, `A`–`Z`), in reading order (upstream's Singles).

A clue kind of two values at cells as upstream's dot runs (`engine/game-id/dot-runs.ts`): a letter a clue, its offset the run of cells before it and its case its value, `cases` the values written lowercase and uppercase. It ends the desc. With `before`, it follows that mark and is written only where a clue is dealt (Pattern's `,`).

A clue kind at cells as upstream's run code of Mosaic: a digit a cell's clue, a letter `a`-`z` a run of 1 to 26 cells without one, the last run written too. With `apart`, a clue is a whole number and `apart` comes between two with no run between them (Range's `_`). `letters` names, by a capital letter, a one-valued kind at cells written in the same stream (Light Up's `B`, a wall with no number).

before.description: Written before the segment, and the segment only where a clue of the kind is dealt (Towers' `,` before its givens).

after.description: By letter, the clue kind whose number may follow the letter, on the letter's cell.

also.description: By number, a one-valued clue kind at a cell written as that number, past the segment's own kind's largest (Bricks' unknown number, `7`).

between.description: What stands between two elements, where not a comma (Towers' `/`).

hidden.description: What an element without a clue is written as, where not nothing (Boats' `-`).

closed.description: A comma after every element, the last too, rather than between two (Boats').

oneOf.description: A clue kind at cells, each clue a capital letter standing for one of its values, between runs of 1 to 26 cells without one written `a`-`z`; a last run is left off (upstream's Boats).

A record a cell, each closed by a comma: the cell's clue of `records` as a number, 0 for none, then a letter `U`, `R`, `D` or `L` for each side whose clue of `sides`, a clue at an edge whose value is one of its ends, has this cell as its value (upstream's Unequal). Where `sides` is instead valued 0 or 1 and complete, the letter is written from both ends of each edge whose clue is 1 (upstream's Adjacent).

A dealt partition as upstream's block structure (`engine/game-id/block-structure.ts`, upstream Keen's and Solo's): the borders between two cells side by side, those inside the rows in reading order and then those between them column by column, as runs of borders inside a part, each a letter `a`-`y` for 1 to 25 before a border between parts, `_` for none and `z` for 25 with none after, and a letter repeated three times or more written once and then the count.
A clue a part of the dealt partition `parts`, in the order of the parts' first cells: the letter of its kind, by `letters`, then its number (upstream Keen's). With `before`, it follows that mark.

tierLetters.description: A fill game's letter for each tier in its params' `d<letter>`, in the tiers' order; absent, each tier's initial, lowercased.

tierFlag.description: A bare letter older game IDs write before the tier for a tier (Light Up's `r`, the recursive solver): read, and never written.

unusedLetters.description: Bare letters older game IDs write for a setting this game has no field for, each after the size or after the tier (Adjacent's `a` after the size, from when upstream dealt it as a mode of Unequal): read, changing nothing, and never written.

tierAliases.description: Retired tier letters older game IDs write after `d`, each read as the tier it names and never written (Bricks' `t`, upstream's Tricky, which dealt only Normal boards).

deal.description: What the generator chooses, in words; `sample` where the deal samples an answer and derives the clues from each kind's `means`, and `hide` where it then hides a kind's clues.

withhold.description: By clue kind at cells, values no deal derives, which only a game ID writes: a value that holds wherever a more telling one does (Boats' segment of unknown shape).

hideFlag.description: A setting the player may turn on, written after the tier by its letter in a full ID, under which the deal hides `kind` too, in one random order with `hide`'s (Boats' `S`, Remove numbers).

never.description: A clue kind, or several, that no deal deals: only a game ID carries one (Pattern's given squares, which only upstream's pictures hold).

latin.description: A clue kind at every cell dealt as a Latin square's numbers, never derived from the answer; each cell holding the value `under` is then numbered again to repeat a number of its row or column, one single in both where there is one (upstream's singles.c `best_black_col`). With no `hide`.

unpair.description: A clue kind at a cell of which two side by side with the same value are both taken off, in reading order: the board's answer is then the one the ladder finds, not the sample. With no `hide`.

hide.description: A clue kind the deal hides from the answer's, or several hidden in one random order, a tier at a time from the lowest: the clues the finishing ladder never read go first, then each other, in a random order, is taken off while the board still finishes at the tier.

hideInTurn.description: The kinds of `hide` go in turn, in its order, at each tier: every clue of one that may go is tried before any of the next, each kind's in a random order (upstream towers.c's givens, then its clues).

hideFrom.description: By kind of `hide`, the tier from which the deal hides it: a board below that tier shows every clue of the kind (Towers' clues at Easy).

hideWhole.description: By kind of `hide`, a board on which the deal hides every clue of it: one below the tier `below` and within the size bounds given beside it, as `play.bounds` states them. The answer is drawn again until the board finishes without the kind (upstream towers.c's Easy boards up to 5x5, which show no given).

oneIn.description: By clue kind at cells, a formula of `at` giving the cells it is the one clue of: the deal shows one in each such group, at a random member, valued as its meaning holds with it the only clue of its kind (Sticks' number, one on each line). Its meaning may then read its own kind's clues.

options.description: Settings the params give that only the deal reads, by name, each written in a full game ID as its letter and a number: a number from `min` to `max`, or with `choices` the index of one, each choice with its `bounds` on the board's size, of which `square` asks a square board, and its `words` in a board's name. Neither is offered on the preset menu but as a board names it after its `WxH` (`7x7s4`).

words.description: A number's words in a board's name where it is not the default, `{n}` the number.

divide.description: A dealt partition divided at random into small parts, apart from the answer (upstream keen.c): each square in a random order joined, at odds `pairs`, to its first neighbor in that order still alone; then each square left alone joined to its first neighboring part of fewer than `most` squares, the draw thrown away where one is left alone still.

oneKind.description: One clue a part of the clue kinds at a dealt partition, dealt from those the answer derives there: the kinds in turn, in `kinds`' order and over and over, each to the first part in a random order that holds none yet and where its clue is not poor, or else where it is; until a round deals none (upstream keen.c's even mix). `poor` and `never` are formulas of the part `at` and the clue's value `v`; a poor clue may be poor only from a tier (`from`), and a clue `never` refuses is not dealt.

onlyFlag.description: A setting the player may turn on, written after the tier by its letter in a full ID, under which `oneKind` deals `kinds` alone (Keen's `m`, multiplication only).

grow.description: A dealt partition grown round the sampled answer: a part round each cell of the sample's value, joined until each holds `holds` of them; one of the answer's pieces of `holds` cells in `closed.oneIn[tier]` dealt as a part of its own, at most one part in `closed.atMostOneIn`, and none without `closed`; no other part under `smallest` cells; then the parts mended until the ladder finishes the board at the tier and not at the tier below. `holds`, `smallest` and `parts` are each a number or a formula of the board's sizes.

parts.description: How many parts a board has, where the rules fix it: a desc with another count is refused.

stripFrom.description: A search tier's deal strips every draw from every clue, and not from a board of the lowest tier but one draw in eight: quicker where the lowest tier's boards leave the search little to strip (Sticks').

symmetric.description: The clues `hide` leaves are symmetric under a half turn of the board: a clue whose partner square has none goes first, and each other goes with its partner.

thorough.description: A setting the player may turn off, written in the params as its letter and 1 or 0: on, the hide tries every clue; off, as many as the board's shorter side, which deals a large board sooner. It is on by default on a board narrower than `offFrom` squares.

oneOf.description: The answer built by the ladder: a random value on a random undecided cell, or `build.value` alone, then every cell the whole ladder decides from those, until every cell is decided. With `first`, a value is dealt first on the share of the cells option `share` gives, as a percentage, as symmetric as option `symmetry` asks (upstream's set_blacks, the choices none, 2-way mirror, 2-way rotational, 4-way mirror and 4-way rotational), and the build is on the clues those cells deal with every clue of `hide` hidden.

order.description: The cells taken in turn, and not at random: the rows from the bottom, each from the left (Bricks' wall, laid on what is below it).

share.description: The chance a cell that may still hold `value` takes it; otherwise it takes another value it may hold, and every cell is decided in turn.

least.description: The least share of the cells no clue fixes that the answer gives `value`: a sample short of it is drawn again.

oneOf.description: The answer as a picture (upstream's pattern.c `generate`): random noise smoothed by one averaging pass over each cell's eight neighbors, `value` at and above its median and `rest` below; a row or column across a side over two cells all one value is drawn again.
The answer as a Latin square of the board's side (upstream's latin.c `latin_generate`): each value once in every row and column, the values the answer's domain from 1.

The answer as `play.tally`'s pieces (upstream's boats.c `boats_generate_fleet`): each a straight run of `value` as long as its length, the longest first, at a random place in a random stretch of a row or column holding no piece, none touching another even at a corner; `rest` on every other cell.
The answer as dominoes of `value`, two cells side by side, none touching another along a side, packed densely by a refill; `rest` on every other cell.
The answer as `count` cells of `value` in every row and column, none within `apart` of another, at random; `rest` on every other cell. `count` is a number or a size the params give.
The answer sampled: `scatter`'s value on a share of the cells, optionally none within `apart` of another; `partner`'s value beside each, along `along`, the two matched; `rest` on every other cell.

each.description: Each cell takes the value at `share`'s chance, so how many do varies from answer to answer; with no `apart` and no `partner`.

tried.description: The share is of the cells tried, in a random order, each taken where it may be: how many are taken varies, and a draw never fails for want of room.

joinedRest.description: A cell is taken only where the cells not taken stay one group, side by side.

mend.description: Where a rule breaks at a cell of the sample, its clues derived from it, the first such cell takes the other of `scatter`'s value and `rest`, until none breaks (upstream's clusters.c). With `each`.

climb.description: Each draw after one the deal refused keeps the cells the ladder decided on it and samples the rest, one draw in a hundred sampling every cell; a board the tier below finishes has one cell turned to the other value. A hill climb toward a board of the tier (upstream's clusters.c). With `each`, and no `hide`.

first.description: A value dealt first, the scatter of `each` drawing every other cell (Sticks' blocks).

noBareLine.description: Draw again an answer with a row or column holding nothing but `rest`: such a line's clue gives it away, and it reads as an empty strip of the board (upstream's Tents).

words.description: What the game says that is not the lexicon's, compiled into the module as `WORDS`: the engine's hint words read it, so a game's code declares none.

cell.description: What the game calls a board position, where its genre says "cell" and not the default "square".

value.description: What the game calls a value, `{valueNoun}` in a hint's words, where it is not the default "number" (Towers' heights).

alongside.description: How a deduction's cells share a unit with the one it decides, in the game's units; default "in line with".

kindWords.description: What a kind of rule's parameters (`src/describe/kinds.ts`) are in this game, said once: the value a count leaves the rest, the words for what is held. Each placement's `with` adds to these or overrides them, and a name a kind does not take is ignored for it.

names.description: What a player calls each technique, keyed by its id or by a rung it is recorded under (a library's technique by its rung): Check & save names the deduction a move followed from by it. Every technique on the ladder needs one; a short noun phrase, lowercase, that reads after "follows from".

phrases.description: Clause source a step's or a technique's clause says by name, `{name}`, written once: the loader puts it in place before the clause is checked, so a phrase holds what a clause may and names the terms of the clause that says it. A phrase may say another; a term named like a phrase is refused.

tiers.description: The ladder, lowest first; the last is the search where the game has one.

rulesOut.description: What a placement rules out at a glance, which the app's auto-cross preference makes for the player: the preference's words, the value a placement gives a square, and the techniques whose conclusions a placement brings. The engine runs the techniques on the board after the move, and the move brings the conclusions of the firings that read a square it placed, on the squares the move left alone. Each technique says what it reads (`marks.reads`).

placing.description: The value a placement gives a square, as the answer's domain reads it.

techniques.description: Ids of the game's own techniques, or `<id>.<arm>` for the firings of one of a technique's `says.arms`: how a technique that also places is named for the arm that only rules out (Tents' `lineCount.countMet`).

scales.description: Grading scales besides `tiers`, each graded and capped on its own, by name: each its tiers, lowest first. A technique on one names one of its tiers.

steps.description: Kinds of hint step the game's own planner emits, which no technique's firing is: a note placed, a move chosen. Each declares what its sentence reads, the terms and marks the planner supplies, and its clauses, which the compiler checks as a technique's are. The planner names the kind and the wording is the first whose `when` holds.

ring.description: The sort of the elements the step decides, which `{ring}` marks; or the sorts, where it decides elements of several (Numgame's two numbers and sign), each named by a reference (`{ring sign: …}`).

terms.description: Named values the planner supplies: `number`, said by the game's value words; `flag`, which an `{if flag: yes | no}` and a wording's `when` read; `unit`, a row, column, block or diagonal, said as its name by `{term}`; `word`, a word the planner makes, said as it is by `{term}` (Wordguess's guess); `values`, several numbers `{term}` says as a list by the game's value words, and whose count form `{term: one | several}` reads how many; a list of words, one of which the planner supplies and `{term}` says as it is (Netslide's tile shapes); or `{ clause: [steps] }`, the move of one of the steps named, which the planner names with what that step is told by and `{term}` says in place, its references with it (Slant's reasons a pair can't both slant one way); or `{ clauses: [steps] }`, several such moves `{term}` says as a list, "a, b and c" (Ascent's numbers a square must be near).

marks.description: The sorts of the elements the planner marks in each role, which a reference names (`{outline cell: ...}`); a mark's size is read in a `when` as `|outlineCell|`. `strike` marks the notes a step rules out (Wordguess's letters).

aim.description: What the move works toward, said first as "Working on …:" (Fifteen's "tile 3"); with no `look` and no `effect`, the move serves it.

answers.description: How the move answers a danger the `look` names, said before it: "L. One way to avoid it: M." (Same Game's).

effect.description: What the move does, where no rule forces it: said after the move as an `effect` relation (Slide's "that makes room for the outlined block").

again.description: A later leg's reasoning, said after its move where the planner says the step is one (`later`): an `again` relation (ABCD's "the same striped row").

variations.description: Blocks added to the description, or replacing its blocks of the same name, under the name the game offers it by: a modifier's words, or a ruleset's name. A variation that only adds is a modifier, and one that replaces is a ruleset. The compiler reads the description with every variation applied, so a technique may read what one deals, and finds it empty on a board without it.

space.description: Partitions of new names, units after the description's, and the diagonals.

position.description: A planning game's layers of new names, each all zeros on a board without the variation.

finish.description: A planning game's finish formulas, true of a finished position where the variation is on.

moves.description: Assignments added to a planning game's moves, by the move's name, made where the variation is on.

clues.description: Clue kinds of the same names, each replaced whole: Rect's Patches widens its number to a question mark.

position.description: A planning game's layers of the same names, replaced.
